barriers.description: Legal COVID-19 restrictions forced focus groups to be conducted online, constraining in-person user engagement.
barriers.justification: Holding focus groups online limited designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and to study user context in person, hindering management of user understanding and requirement specification.
barriers.reference_excerpt: At that time, legal restrictions due to the COVID-19 pandemic prohibited on-site meetings. Thus, all focus groups were performed online.

barriers.description: A target user group (lung cancer support group) could not attend on-site usability sessions, reducing the number of participating groups.
barriers.justification: The absence of this group reduced participant diversity and limited the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and collect representative usability data across contexts of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Since the app was provided on a test device for the second stage of usability testing, on-site meetings were necessary. As the lung cancer support group could not participate in meetings on-site, the number of participating groups reduced.

barriers.description: Participants without a private mobile device could not take part because the study could not provide smartphones.
barriers.justification: Excluding those without devices constrained recruitment and limited designers' ability to evaluate the app across the full user population and contexts of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: As the app needed to be installed on a private mobile device, participants without a mobile device could not take part, as no one in the study could be provided with a smartphone.

barriers.description: The study failed to reach the planned ≥15 users for usability test 2, despite exceeding smaller critical thresholds.
barriers.justification: Insufficient participant numbers reduced statistical power and limited designers' ability to robustly evaluate and iterate on designs, hindering evaluation and integration of feedback.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Although the critical number of 5 persons was exceeded, the overall target of ≥15 users per usability test was not reached.

barriers.description: A coding error in the randomization prevented balanced assignment to app versions, producing uneven group sizes.
barriers.justification: This implementation error directly prevented planned group comparisons and therefore constrained the designers' ability to evaluate the effect of add-on features, hindering evaluation and iteration workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Due to an error in the code, the randomized assignment of participants into the 3 versions (A, B, and C) did not lead to the same group size. Due to the uneven distribution of participants in the 3 app versions, group comparisons could not be performed.

barriers.description: A low number of male participants prevented sex-stratified analyses in some tests.
barriers.justification: Imbalanced gender participation limited designers' ability to analyze subgroup differences and to understand varied user experiences, hindering evaluation and requirement specification for different user groups.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Since the number of male participants was below the critical sum of 5 users, no further analysis stratified by sex was performed.

barriers.description: Older participants submitted fewer questionnaire responses, reducing data completeness for that subgroup.
barriers.justification: Age-related lower response rates constrained designers' ability to evaluate engagement and to understand usage patterns across ages, hindering management of user understanding and evaluation workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Thus, the higher the age of the participant, the fewer the questionnaire responses submitted.
